title: RAG architectures
summary: Retrieve external evidence and condition generation on a bounded set of source passages.
why: Supplies information absent from model weights and makes source attribution possible.
interview: Separate retrieval failure, evidence insufficiency, and unsupported generation.
derivation: The marginalization equation describes latent-document RAG. Many production pipelines instead concatenate a reranked evidence set into one prompt. Keep those implementations distinct.
Evaluate retrieval recall separately from grounded-answer quality. ACL and tenant filters must apply before evidence reaches the generator.

steps.note: Expansion or HyDE can improve recall but can introduce drift.
Use metadata constraints and hybrid lexical/vector candidates.
Cross-encoder scores cost per candidate; deduplicate evidence.
steps.transformation: score(query, chunk); truncate to token budget

steps.note: Verify that cited passages support the actual claim.

traps: Similarity is not truth or access authorization.
Chunk boundaries can split the fact from its qualifier.
A low-confidence retriever score is not calibrated answer uncertainty.
tradeoff: Reranking improves precision at additional latency; expansion increases recall and candidate cost.

variants.title: Naive RAG
variants.flow: query -> embedding -> top-k chunks -> prompt -> answer
variants.detail: Baseline for measuring the value of each added stage.

variants.title: Advanced / modular RAG
variants.flow: query expansion / HyDE -> hybrid retrieval -> rerank -> context compression -> generation
variants.detail: Modules can be composed and evaluated independently.

variants.title: Self-RAG
variants.flow: input -> retrieve? -> passage -> generate -> critique/support tokens -> selected answer
variants.detail: Reflection tokens are learned behavior in the Self-RAG method, not a guarantee from adding a reflection prompt.

variants.title: Corrective RAG
variants.flow: retrieve -> evaluator -> correct / ambiguous / incorrect -> refine or web fallback -> generate
variants.detail: Fallback needs trusted sources, access checks, and an explicit latency budget.

explanations.title: Naive, advanced, and modular RAG
paragraphs: Ingestion extracts source text, chunks it with stable IDs, embeds chunks, and indexes vectors with metadata. At query time the retriever returns candidates; the generator receives a bounded evidence set and produces an answer with source references. Ingestion and answering have different freshness and latency requirements.

Naive RAG embeds the original question, retrieves top-k chunks, and concatenates them. Advanced RAG may rewrite the question, combine sparse and dense candidates, deduplicate, rerank, and compress evidence. Modular RAG makes those operations replaceable or conditional instead of prescribing one fixed pipeline.

A cross-encoder scores the question and candidate passage jointly. Reranking a small candidate set costs less than cross-encoding the whole corpus. Query expansion improves recall but can dilute intent. HyDE embeds a hypothetical answer document; that generated text is a retrieval aid, not verified answer evidence.
explanations.flow:
sources -> chunks + provenance -> embeddings + index
question -> rewrite / HyDE -> sparse + dense candidates
-> ACL filter -> rerank -> evidence budget -> generate + citations

explanations.title: Self-RAG and Corrective RAG
paragraphs: Self-RAG trains a model to use retrieval and critique tokens that control retrieval and assess evidence relevance, support, and answer utility. Adding a generic self-reflection prompt to an ordinary pipeline does not reproduce that training procedure.

Corrective RAG evaluates retrieval quality and chooses whether to retain, refine, or replace retrieved evidence, including web-search fallback. A retrieval score is not a calibrated probability that an answer is correct. Learn or validate thresholds on representative queries.

Both approaches need budgets and termination rules. Repeated retrieval can improve coverage while increasing latency and introducing conflicting evidence. A failed evidence check should permit an explicit insufficient-evidence response instead of forcing an answer.

explanations.title: Separate retrieval, evidence selection, and answer quality
paragraphs: For a held-out question, first ask whether the relevant source exists in the corpus. Then measure retrieval recall@k, reranker quality, context precision, answer correctness, and support for each cited claim. These measurements isolate which stage failed.

Suppose a question needs two passages and only one reaches the prompt. The language model may produce a fluent unsupported join. Increasing generation temperature cannot repair missing evidence. Increase retrieval coverage or explicitly identify the missing fact.

Apply access rules before content reaches the model, including through query expansion, graph traversal, caches, and observability logs. Preserve document versions and offsets so a citation resolves to the text used for the answer. Retrieved text is untrusted data and can contain instructions that conflict with the task.
